title: Verbal Aspect (Advanced)
intro: At A2 you learned that imperfective describes process/repetition while perfective describes completed results. At B1, we go deeper: aspect choice depends on context, not just 'completion.' Imperfective can describe a completed action if you're focusing on the activity itself (Вчера я читал книгу - I was reading yesterday). Perfective emphasizes the result or a single bounded event (Я прочитал книгу - I finished reading the book). Mastering aspect means understanding WHAT you want to emphasize, not just whether something finished.
rules: Imperfective focuses on PROCESS, DURATION, or REPETITION: Я долго писал письмо. (I wrote the letter for a long time.)
Perfective focuses on RESULT, COMPLETION, or SINGLE EVENT: Я написал письмо. (I wrote/finished the letter.)
With time expressions: долго/часто/всегда → imperfective; вдруг/наконец/уже → often perfective.
Negation often prefers imperfective (general denial): Я не читал эту книгу. (I haven't read this book.)
General experience uses imperfective: 'Ты читал эту книгу?' = Have you ever read this book? The focus is on whether the experience happened, not on completion.
examples: Что ты делал вчера? — Я читал. (What did you do? — I was reading.), process/activity
Ты прочитал книгу? — Да, прочитал. (Did you finish the book? — Yes, I did.), result
Она долго готовила обед. (She cooked dinner for a long time.), duration → impf
Она приготовила обед. (She made/finished dinner.), result → pf

items.prompt: Я долго _____ это письмо. (I wrote this letter for a long time.)
items.promptEnglish: I wrote this letter for a long time.
items.hint: Долго (for a long time) emphasizes duration → imperfective

items.prompt: Наконец я _____ эту задачу! (Finally I solved this problem!)
Раньше каждый день он _____ газету. (Every day he used to read the newspaper.)
items.promptEnglish: He used to read the newspaper every day.
items.hint: Каждый день (every day) = repeated action → imperfective
items.explanation: Repetition marker 'каждый день' requires imperfective: читал.

items.prompt: — Что ты делал вечером? — Я _____ фильм. (What did you do? I watched a film.)
items.promptEnglish: What did you do in the evening? - I watched a film.
items.hint: Answering 'what were you doing' describes the activity → imperfective
items.explanation: Describing what you were doing (activity) = imperfective: смотрел.

items.prompt: Ты уже _____ домашнее задание? (Have you already done the homework?)
items.promptEnglish: Have you already done the homework?
items.hint: Уже (already) asks about completed result → perfective
items.explanation: Result question with 'уже' requires perfective: сделал.

items.prompt: Вдруг он _____ и ушёл. (Suddenly he got up and left.)
items.promptEnglish: Suddenly he got up and left.
items.explanation: Single sudden action with 'вдруг' requires perfective: встал.

items.prompt: Я не _____ эту книгу. (I haven't read this book.)
items.hint: General negation (never did X) prefers imperfective
items.explanation: General denial of experience uses imperfective: не читал.

items.prompt: Он весь день _____ отчёт. (He wrote the report all day.)
items.promptEnglish: He wrote the report all day.
items.hint: Весь день (all day) emphasizes duration → imperfective
items.explanation: Duration marker 'весь день' requires imperfective: писал.

items.prompt: Она _____ торт и поставила его на стол. (She baked a cake and put it on the table.)
items.promptEnglish: She baked a cake and put it on the table.
items.explanation: Completed action in sequence requires perfective: испекла.

blanks: Вчера я три часа _____ уроки. (Yesterday I did homework for three hours.)
Я долго _____ это письмо. (I wrote this letter for a long time.)
Она наконец _____ обед. (She finally finished cooking dinner.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Duration (три часа, долго) requires imperfective; result (наконец) requires perfective
hints: 'Долго' emphasizes the process over time. Which aspect?
'Наконец' (finally) emphasizes reaching a result. Which aspect?
explanations: Duration markers require imperfective: делал (was doing for three hours).
Duration with 'долго' requires imperfective: писал (was writing for a long time).
'Наконец' signals a completed result, requiring perfective: приготовила (finished cooking).

minimalPairs.context: — Ты читал «Войну и мир»? — Нет, не _____.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Have you read War and Peace? - No, I haven't.
minimalPairs.explanation: General experience question/denial uses imperfective: читал.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Did you finish the book? - Yes, already finished.
minimalPairs.explanation: Asking about completion → answer confirms result: прочитал.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort these markers by which aspect they typically require

reviewVocab.example: Я долго читал. Весь день работал.
